post.caption: Dürer trained as a goldsmith first. His father, a goldsmith, settled in Nuremberg in 1455. Albrecht later wrote that his father taught him the goldsmith's craft. In 1484, at age 13, he drew himself in silverpoint, which uses a metal stylus on prepared paper so lines cannot be erased. In 1486 he began a three year apprenticeship with a painter. He later wrote that painting drew him more than goldsmith's work. A British Museum drawing shows a table fountain he probably designed, meant for his father-in-law to build. Its jets were colored red, for red wine.
